The mass/volume in Serum or Plasma (mg/dL) is concept 3001420 — the right one for the "1.6 mg/dL" threshold. Now let me run the full analysis: identify new PPI users (first-ever PPI exposure) and check for serum magnesium < 1.6 mg/dL within 90 days.

arguments.sql_query:
WITH ppi_desc AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ca.descendant_concept_id AS concept_id
  FROM omop.concept_ancestor ca
  WHERE ca.ancestor_concept_id = 21600095
),
first_ppi AS (
  SELECT de.person_id, MIN(de.drug_exposure_start_date) AS index_date
  FROM omop.drug_exposure de
  JOIN ppi_desc p ON p.concept_id = de.drug_concept_id
  GROUP BY de.person_id
),
mg AS (
  SELECT m.person_id, m.measurement_date, m.value_as_number
  FROM omop.measurement m
  WHERE m.measurement_concept_id = 3001420
    AND m.value_as_number IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
  COUNT(DISTINCT fp.person_id) AS new_ppi_users,
  COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN mg.person_id IS NOT NULL THEN fp.person_id END) AS users_with_mg_measured_in_window,
  COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN mg.value_as_number < 1.6 THEN fp.person_id END) AS users_with_low_mg_in_window
FROM first_ppi fp
LEFT JOIN mg
  ON mg.person_id = fp.person_id
 AND mg.measurement_date >= fp.index_date
 AND mg.measurement_date <= DATEADD(day, 90, fp.index_date)

content.text: 197,228 patients have a PPI exposure. The full join timed out because the measurement table is large. Let me compute the two window counts directly, joining only within the cohort. I'll first materialize each new user's index date, then join magnesium. To avoid timeout, let me compute the first-exposure date and low-mg count in one query but push the mg filter aggressively.

arguments.sql_query:
WITH first_ppi AS (
  SELECT de.person_id, MIN(de.drug_exposure_start_date) AS index_date
  FROM omop.drug_exposure de
  WHERE de.drug_concept_id IN (
    SELECT ca.descendant_concept_id
    FROM omop.concept_ancestor ca
    WHERE ca.ancestor_concept_id = 21600095
  )
  GROUP BY de.person_id
)
SELECT
  COUNT(DISTINCT fp.person_id) AS users_with_mg_in_90d,
  COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN m.value_as_number < 1.6 THEN fp.person_id END) AS users_with_low_mg_in_90d
FROM first_ppi fp
JOIN omop.measurement m
  ON m.person_id = fp.person_id
 AND m.measurement_concept_id = 3001420
 AND m.value_as_number IS NOT NULL
 AND m.measurement_date >= fp.index_date
 AND m.measurement_date <= DATEADD(day, 90, fp.index_date)

content.text:
## Answer

Among new PPI users (first-ever PPI exposure in the database, n = 197,228):

- **60,230** had a serum magnesium level (LOINC "Magnesium [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma", concept 3001420) recorded within 90 days of starting a PPI.
- **13,748** had at least one serum magnesium **< 1.6 mg/dL** in that window.

So hypomagnesemia (< 1.6 mg/dL) within 90 days was recorded in:
- **~7.0%** of all new PPI users (13,748 / 197,228), and
- **~22.8%** of those who actually had magnesium checked (13,748 / 60,230).

**Method notes**
- New user = first PPI `drug_exposure` (index date) across all PPI descendants of ATC "Proton pump inhibitors" (concept 21600095).
- Window = index date through index + 90 days, inclusive; counted a patient once if any qualifying result fell below threshold.
- Only serum/plasma magnesium in mg/dL (concept 3001420) was used, matching the 1.6 mg/dL unit. Note that only ~31% of new users had this lab checked in-window, so the true prevalence of hypomagnesemia is likely underestimated by the 7% figure (testing is not universal).
